conceptual assets.information: The per-channel enable state determines whether PWM counting and output operate and whether the upstream clock generator is enabled. Channel operation and clocking depend on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: This is sensitive operating configuration that a bus write can modify at line 184. It gates the channel counters and duty progression at lines 212-225 and drives the clock-enable request at line 197, so changing it can disable required PWM operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could clear or alter the channel enable bit, disabling PWM generation and the associated clock-generator enable request.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and clock-divider settings determine which clock-generator rate is used and how many selected ticks form a PWM timebase. PWM timing depends on these stored settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The timebase settings are sensitive operating configuration and are written from bus data at lines 185 and 187, allowing an attacker to change the PWM frequency or timing.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could replace the prescaler or divider values, causing PWM timing to differ from the required configuration.

conceptual assets.information: The polarity and duty-cycle settings define the active level and proportion of each generated PWM period. The waveform produced by the channel depends on these stored settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: These are sensitive waveform configuration values written from bus data at lines 186 and 188, so an attacker can modify the polarity or duty cycle.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could change the polarity or duty value, causing the external PWM-controlled function to receive an incorrect waveform.

conceptual assets.information: The channel-selection decision determines which repeated PWM channel receives a write or supplies a readback. It has no separate entry or exit anchor because it is an internal decode of the bus access address.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The decoded selector determines which channel's write and read enables are asserted at lines 109-111, so a changed address can steer an access to the wrong channel or prevent the intended channel from being accessed. This selector is retained as its own entry-select decision rather than as an access-command field.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue a crafted address that updates or reads a different PWM channel, or selects no channel and withholds the intended access.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel read-enable decision controls whether a channel's stored configuration is presented to the readback path. It has no separate entry or exit anchor because it is derived from bus access-command fields.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The read-enable signal gates the channel readback expression at lines 111 and 194, so manipulating the access decision can suppress the configuration response and block a required read transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress the per-channel read-enable condition so that configuration read requests return no channel data.

conceptual assets.information: The generated PWM waveform is the timed output used by external circuitry or loads. It is produced inside the channel and leaves the unit through the PWM output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The output waveform is assigned from the enable, duty and polarity decisions at lines 231-234, so altered internal configuration can produce an incorrect waveform. The enable path can reset or suppress waveform operation at lines 212-225, making the output unavailable.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the writable channel settings or disable the channel, causing an incorrect or absent PWM waveform at the output.

considered, not kept.reason: The request strobe, direction and register-selection fields only describe access commands and are excluded as independent information by the access-command-fields rule, except for the separately retained channel selector and readback gate.
The we signals only decode bus access fields to let channel configuration registers accept written data, so they are access-command machinery rather than information of their own.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus response handshake and error status
considered, not kept.reason: The acknowledge and constant error fields only implement bus handshaking or status and do not hold an independent protected value.
The rdata, rdata_sum and response data path only carries the kept channel configuration settings through an OR-based readback and is not information of its own.
The clkgen_i input only supplies a condition that advances the PWM counters, so it is a pacing input rather than a conceptual asset of its own.
The counter and tick registers only sequence and pace PWM steps, so the pacing-pulse and sequencing-state rules exclude them as independent information.
The clk_i and rstn_i inputs only time or reset the channel and response state, and clocks and resets are excluded as conceptual assets.
NUM_CHANNELS is a build-time generic that cannot be changed or withheld at run time, so the build-time-values rule excludes it.
